column3: The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB condenses these to “said.”
The Hebrew ends with another “saying” after the LORD’s command; BSB omits that repetition.
The Hebrew repeats the slaughtering verb and “the camp”; BSB states the slaughtering verb once and replaces the second “camp” with “it.”
The Hebrew says blood “shall be reckoned to that man” and repeats “that man”; BSB says he “shall incur bloodguilt” and then uses a pronoun.
The Hebrew places the sacrifices “over the face of the field,” with singular “field”; BSB says “in the open fields.”
The Hebrew uses a present participle for their prostitution after the goat demons; BSB uses “have prostituted themselves.”
The Hebrew ends with plural “his peoples”; BSB uses singular “his people.”
The Hebrew repeats “the person eating the blood”; BSB uses “that person.”
The Hebrew says the blood makes atonement “by the life”; BSB says “for the soul.”
The Hebrew says “I have said”; BSB uses present “I say.”
The Hebrew repeats the hunting root in “hunts game”; BSB says “hunts down” an animal or bird.
The Hebrew repeats “all flesh” three times and includes “with its life” in the first clause; BSB varies the middle occurrence as “any living thing” and omits the additional life phrase.
The Hebrew joins the dead and torn animal categories with “and” and leaves the tearing agent unnamed; BSB uses “or” and specifies “by wild beasts.”
The Hebrew says to wash “his flesh” and leaves the object of the first washing verb unstated; BSB uses “bathe himself” and supplies “his clothes.”
